sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2018. A sketch of Northern Akhvakh (2nd draft). Ms. for Koryakov, Lander & Maisak (eds.), The Caucasian Languages: An International Handbook.
sources.note: Prosody section concerns Northern Akhvakh only; for Southern Akhvakh it only notes that Magomedbekova 1967 'also includes some data on Southern Akhvakh' and that Southern forms are quoted from Magomedova & Abdulaeva 2007.

sources.citation: Kibrik, A. E. & S. V. Kodzasov. 1990. Sopostavitel'noe izuchenie dagestanskix jazykov. Imja. Fonetika. Moscow: MGU (Akhvakh sketch pp. 322-323).
sources.note: Akhvakh data are from Tad-Magitl' (Northern): 'Slovesnoe udarenie otsutstvuet..' plus syllabic tones; no southern village sampled.

sources.citation: Institut jazykoznanija RAN, project 'Malye jazyki Rossii': page 'Juzhnoaxvaxskij jazyk' (data supplied by I. A. Abdulaeva and N. A. Muravyev), minlang.iling-ran.ru, accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Phonetics paragraph gives inventory only (5 vowel phonemes with long/nasalised allophones, 48 consonants); nothing on stress. Bibliography names Magomedbekova 1962, 1967, Abdulaeva 2001 and a forthcoming English grammar sketch by Muravyev.

sources.citation: Borise, Lena. 2020. Word stress in the languages of the Caucasus (lingbuzz 004203), sec. 7.2.
sources.note: Summarises conflicting accounts of Akhvakh stress (Magomedova & Abdulaeva 2007: 657-659; Creissels 2010; Kodzasov tonal analysis) -- all Northern Akhvakh; no statement specific to the southern varieties.

sources.citation: Muravyev, N. A. 2017. Semantika lokativnyx padezhnyx form v ratlubskom govore juzhnoaxvaxskogo jazyka. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana XIII(1): 725-750.
sources.note: Nothing (case semantics; transcriptions carry no accent marks; a full-text search for stress/accent udaren/akcent/stress = 0).

sources.citation: Magomedbekova, Z. M. 1999. Axvaxskij jazyk. In Alekseev, M. E. (ed.), Jazyki mira: Kavkazskie jazyki, 252-261. Moscow: Academia.
sources.note: Sec. 2.0.0 is explicitly 'dannye severnogo dialekta'; 2.1.2 (p. 254) 'Udarenie slaboe, dinamicheskoe, nefiksirovannoe' therefore describes Northern Akhvakh. Sec. 2.7.0 (pp. 259-261) on the southern dialect (Ratlub closest to northern, Tljanub transitional, Cegob most divergent) lists vowel/consonant, case and verb differences but says nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Magomedbekova, Z. M. 1962. O foneticheskix osobennostjax juzhnogo dialekta axvaxskogo jazyka. Iberijsko-kavkazskoe jazykoznanie (Tbilisi) XIII: 281-284.
sources.note: 4-page primary note on Southern Akhvakh phonetics (mainly Cegob data): loss/spirantisation of the 'soft' affricates, vowel reduction in Tljanub and Cegob, word-final consonants r l m n b allowed in Tljanub/Cegob. No stress section; the only stress-related remark (printed p. 284): 'V cegobskom i tljanubskom govorax v konce slova vmesto bezudarnogo o severnogo dialekta vystupaet u' (word-final o of the northern dialect, described as unstressed, corresponds to u) -- not a placement rule.

sources.citation: Magomedbekova, Z. M. 1955. Voprosy fonetiki axvaxskogo jazyka. Iberijsko-kavkazskoe jazykoznanie VII. Tbilisi.
sources.note: Her full phonetics article (Northern-based) -- the original locus of the 'weak, dynamic, non-fixed stress' characterisation; open at Iverieli but not downloaded (250 MB volume, relevance to the southern varieties indirect).

sources.citation: Muravyev, N. A. (forthcoming). Grammatical sketch of Southern Akhvakh (in English; announced on minlang.iling-ran.ru, presumably for Koryakov, Lander & Maisak eds., The Caucasian Languages: An International Handbook, De Gruyter).
